This is likely a convulsion or seizure, commonly caused in children by high fever from malaria or other infections, but meningitis, low blood sugar, epilepsy, or severe illness can also cause it.  
Lay the child on the side, remove dangerous objects, loosen tight clothing, and do not put a spoon, hand, water, herbs, or medicine into the mouth during the seizure.  
If there is fever, expose the child, sponge with lukewarm water, and give paracetamol only after the child is fully awake and able to swallow.  
Take the child urgently to a hospital, especially if the shaking lasts more than 5 minutes, happens again, the child is less than 6 months old, remains unconscious, has neck stiffness, vomiting, poor feeding, or signs of malaria or infection.  
The hospital may check blood sugar, malaria test, temperature, and treat the cause, with emergency seizure medicine if needed.
